t: Pedestrian safety improvements near schools
rt: MOTION, submitted by Councilmembers Sittenfeld, Landsman, Seelbach, Mann, Pastor, Dennard, Young, Murray and Vice Mayor Smitherman, Whereas Cincinnati City Council remain strongly committed to pedestrian safety, including through its allocation of $500,000 in FY2018 and a proposed $500,000 as part of the budget for FY2019; and WHEREAS Cincinnati City Council desires to be an exemplary partner to our local educations institutions, including Cincinnati Public Schools and recognizes that pedestrian safety is a critical issue for the safety of the city's youth; WE MOVE  that the City Administration work with the Cincinnati Public Schools Administration to analyze and prioritize pedestrian safety hot spots near and around schools; and WE MOVE that the City Administration report back on this coordination effort in 90 days; and WE MOVE that some portion of the $500,000 FY2019 allocation is used for pedestrian safety improvements that impact areas with high concentrations of school-age children or that are particularly dangerous pedestrians areas used by school-aged children.
sm: Coordinate with schools to analyze pedestrian safety hotspots and implement improvements.

t: Dream Campus development project New Friendship Baptist Church
rt: MOTION, submitted by Vice Mayor Smitherman, Councilmembers Young, Pastor, Murray and Mann, WE MOVE that the City Administration begin to engage New Friendship Baptist Church (3212 Reading Rd. 45229) and Temple Bible College (3202 Reading Rd. 45229) in discussions to place a development project in or around both properties with a concept called "The Dream Campus". WE FURTHER MOVE that all building code violations be stopped on both properties and no citations created without the explicit direction of Council except in the case of significant risk of human injury. WE FURTHER MOVE that all economic development tools be shared with both property owners in writing and that recommendations be made on how to move forward with the development "The Dream Campus" in 30 days. WE FURTHER MOVE that the current zoning of both properties be evaluated and recommendations made to the Planning Commission on any zoning changes that need to occur in order to make "The Dream Campus" a reality. WE FURTHER MOVE that the Administration call a meeting at City Hall with the development team of New Friendship Baptist Church, Temple Bible College, Uptown Consortium, Department of Community & Economic Development, City Manager Office, City Solicitor's Office, Planning Commission and Buildings & Inspections Department to discuss the development and report back to Council on an action plan on how the City of Cincinnati can assist in the development of the footprint. WE FURTHER MOVE that specific discussions around the development of a parking garage using TIF dollars with all or joint ownerships with New Friendship Baptist Church and Temple Bible College which could include expanding the footprint north or south of the two properties by 2.5 acres. WE FURTHER MOVE that the Administration report back to Council with recommendations on a development deal by first meeting after summer recess. (ATTACHMENT)
sm: Directs Administration to engage churches on Dream Campus development with zoning and TIF parking garage.

t: Increase Riverfront Park funding for economic development
rt: MOTION, dated 06/22/2018, submitted by Councilmember Sittenfeld, WHEREAS, City Council invests public resources in our neighborhoods, infrastructure, businesses, and the people of our community with the goal that such allocations will yield a strong return on investment back to the public; WHEREAS, in addition to being a major driver of quality of life, recreation, and tourism, one such shining example of return on investment is Cincinnati's Smale Riverfront Park; WHEREAS, each year, the Park generates revenue from various concerts, festivals, races, private events, and other rentals; WHEREAS, because of this model of sustainability, the Park's revenue-generation increasingly can cover expenses that historically have been addressed from the City's General Fund; WHEREAS, this positive sustainability un-encumbers General Fund dollars for other strategic allocations with a similar goal of yielding return on investment back to the public; THEREFORE, WE MOVE that due to the success of the Smale Riverfront Park, the appropriation of the Fund 329 Riverfront Park will be increased by $500,000 to fund direct expenditures of the Park, thereby reducing the General Fund Budget to be reallocated toward high-potential, high-ROI programming within our Innovation Ecosystem, specifically, allocating $300,000 to Cintrifuse, and $200,000 to CincyTech, which will, in turn, automatically leverage an additional half-million dollars in matching funds from the State of Ohio.

t: Emergency vehicle idling near greenspaces feasibility report
rt: MOTION, submitted by Councilmembers Dennard, Landsman and Seelbach, WHEREAS emergency vehicles such as police cars, ambulances and fire trucks, along with other services vehicles such as armored cars, are in an ideal position to save fuel and reduce emissions with technologies and best practices that allow them to perform vital services without idling. WE MOVE that the Administration report to Council on the  feasibility of prohibiting emergency vehicles from standing and/or idling near greenspaces in the City of Cincinnati, whether in the downtown section or otherwise, for a period in excess of 15 minutes. WE FURTHER MOVE that the Administration include in its report the feasibility of implementing fuel and emissions reduction technologies recommended in 2015 report by the U.S. Department of Energy titled, "Idling Reduction for Emergency and Other Service Vehicles". WE FURTHER MOVE for the purpose of this motion, the terms STANDING and IDLING are to be defined under administrative regulations adopted by the Ohio Department of Transportation.
sm: Request administration report on prohibiting emergency vehicle idling near greenspaces

t: Cincinnati Bell Connector streetcar SORTA operator management evaluation
rt: MOTION, submitted by Vice Mayor Smitherman, WE MOVE that the City Administration evaluate options for removing the Southwest Ohio Regional Transit Authority ("SORTA") from its role as the operator of the City's streetcar system and establish direct City management of the Cincinnati Bell Connector. In order to allow for an informed debate on the merits of terminating SORTA as operator, we request the Administration answer the following questions: 1. Does SORTA desire to continue operating the streetcar? 2. What are the estimated budget (personnel, equipment) cost and indirect costs for the City to assume direct management of the Cincinnati Bell Connector? 3. What is the Federal Transit Administration's role in any such decision and do we know its general position on such a change? 4. What legal or contract considerations are necessary to be considered as part of this discussion? 5. What would be the steps and approximate timeline required to negotiate the termination of SORTA as operator and assume direct City management of the streetcar system? 6. What other considerations, if any should the City take into account?
sm: Evaluate removing SORTA from streetcar operation establish direct city management

t: Council at-large staggered terms Charter amendment
rt: ORDINANCE, (EMERGENCY) submitted by Councilmember Greg Landsman, from Paula Boggs Muething, City Solicitor, TO SUBMIT to the electors of the City of Cincinnati an amendment to the Charter of the City to provide that, effective as of the general election of November 2021, the members of Council shall be elected at-large for staggered four-year terms, which shall commence as of the January 2022 Council term, with five members of Council serving four-year terms and four members of Council serving two year terms, and thereafter, all Councilmembers will serve four-year terms which shall occur on a staggered basis, with elections for either four or five designated Council positions being held every two years, by amending existing Sections 4 and 5a of Article II, "Legislative Power," Section 3 of Article III, "Mayor," and Section 1, 2a, 2b, 3, 5a, and 8 of Article IX, "Nominations and Elections."

t: Income Tax and Sales Tax Ballot Measure
rt: ORDINANCE, (EMERGENCY) submitted by Councilmember Jeff Pastor, from Paula Boggs Muething, City Solicitor, SUBMITTING to the Cincinnati electorate a ballot measure modifying the provisions of Chapter 311, "City of Cincinnati Income Tax," by amending Section 311-3, Purposes; Imposition of Tax; Tax Rates," of the Cincinnati Municipal Code, on the condition that at the general election on November 6, 2018 the electors of Hamilton County approve the levy of a sales and use tax to provide general revenues for the Southwest Ohio Regional Transit Authority, to reduce a portion of the earned income tax from two percent (2%) down to one and seven-tenths percent (1.7%), and to provide for an additional tax of one tenth of one percent (0.1%) on earned income for the following purposes: 0.033% per year to be used for street improvements; 0.033% per year for permanent improvements for parks and recreation facilities, including new facilities; .017% per year toward human services funding; 0.011% per year for permanent improvements promoting economic development in census tracks where 30% or more of the residents live in poverty; and 0.006% per year for community councils and neighborhood business district investment programs.
sm: Reduce income tax, add dedicated taxes for streets, parks, human services, economic development

t: Property Tax Working Group Senior Citizens Fixed Income
rt: MOTION, submitted by Vice Mayor Smitherman and Councilmembers Mann, Dennard and Young WE MOVE that the lobbyist for the City of Cincinnati provide a procedural framework for City Council and the Property Tax Project working group to amend Ohio state laws governing property taxes to ensure that property owners, specifically legacy residents and senior citizens on fixed incomes, who reside in developing neighborhoods and whose property taxes are increasing as a result have a greater opportunity to remain in their homes. WE FURTHER MOVE that a working group be created to study trends related to property taxes, especially the issue of rising property taxes in areas experiencing significant levels of development; to make recommendations to City Council aimed at helping to keep senior citizens in their homes and communities; and to report on best practices in other cities and states facing similar challenges. WE FURTHER MOVE that the working group include members from: the African-American Chamber of Commerce; the Board of Realtors; the Cincinnati Neighborhood Business Districts United; the Community Action Agency; the Community Development Corporations Association of Greater Cincinnati; the Council on Aging; the Baptist Ministers Conference; the Hamilton County Auditor/representative; the Homebuilders Association; Invest in Neighborhoods; representatives of Allied Construction Industries; the United Way; the University of Cincinnati's Real Estate Program and the DAAAP School of Planning; and the Urban League. WE FURTHER MOVE that the working group review the City's Tax Abatement Program. WE FURTHER MOVE that the Planning Department lead this working group.
sm: Create working group to study property tax increases affecting legacy residents

I FURTHER MOVE that the administration investigate the use of more environmentally friendly products to control weed and pests where children and pets play in lieu of chemicals like glyphosate and provide a plan for the use and deployment of more environmentally friendly pesticides/herbicides where people, children and pets play/recreate. t: Cincinnati 2030 District Founding Member Membership
rt: MOTION, submitted by Councilmember Sittenfeld, WHEREAS, Green Umbrella and a number of related partners and entities are launching the Cincinnati 2020 District, a collaborative effort to create a network of healthy, high performing buildings in Cincinnati's Central Business District where property owners will voluntarily commit to collectively reduce their buildings' energy use, water consumption and transportation emissions by the year 2020, making Cincinnati the 21st 2030 District in the country; and WHEREAS, Cincinnati City Council has already demonstrated support for the goals of the 2030 District in connection with the passage of the Green Cincinnati Plan in 2018; and WHEREAS, the City of Cincinnati's revolving energy loan fund provides a resource for the City to undertake projects that fulfill the goals of the 2030 District. THEREFORE, WE MOVE that the Cincinnati City Council encourages property owners in the District to join the initial Cincinnati 2030 District and desires that the City of Cincinnati endeavor to collaborate with other property owners to meet associated goals for the buildings it owns in the 2030 District; and WE MOVE that the City of Cincinnati join the 2030 District as a Founding Member by adding City Hall and the Duke Energy Convention Center to the 2030 District.

t: Kingsley Co. Mt. Auburn hotel CRA abatement approval
rt: MOTION, dated 10/03/2018, submitted by Councilmembers Landsman and Dennard, WE MOVE that the Administration recommend that City Council exercise its discretion under Ordinance No. 275-2017 and approve a 15-year net 60% CRA abatement for the Kingsley + Co. Mt. Auburn hotel investment for the reasons stated herein. This investment warrants a 15-year, net 60% CRA abatement in part because of the nature and size of the investment, and the neighborhood in which the investment will be made, as well as the project's additional commitments to higher wages, local worker hiring preferences, and a youth wellness fund for the neighborhood itself. The census tract where the hotel is being constructed as a 44.4% poverty rate. Over the last five years, the only subsidies that the City has provided in Mt. Auburn have been for housing projects. Kingsley + Co. will create and maintain at least 10 permanent full-time equivalent employees and commit to pay such employees at least $15.00 per hour and such commitment shall be reflected in the related CRA Agreement. Kingsley + Co. are investing $14 million into a commercial project in Mr. Auburn. The city's support of this deal will be the first city subsidy of a Mt. Auburn commercial deal in nearly a decade. Kingsley + Co. is committed to working with its general contractor and neighborhood organizations to identify and hire qualified sub-contractors and laborers from Mt. Auburn, establishing goals as they relate to both inclusion and local hire. Kingsley + Co. through its owner's foundation will use best efforts to provide funding for a youth wellness program at Mt. Auburn's William Howard Taft Elementary School and to work with community stakeholders to create measurable performance goals.
sm: Approve 15-year net 60% CRA abatement for $14 million hotel investment with wage and local hiring commitments.

t: Meet and Confer workforce development policy requirement
rt: MOTION, submitted by Councilmembers Seelbach, Mann, Young, Dennard Landsman and Sittenfeld, WE MOVE that the Administration develop and bring to council policies which add a "Meet & Confer" requirement to the acceptance of city funds by private organizations whereby the funding recipient shall meet & Confer with institutions such as Cincinnati Works to review whether a training, placement & coaching partnership would benefit the funding recipient or its workforce. City funds shall be defined as TIF dollars, operating support funds, capital funds or a Job Creation Tax Credit at a value of over $500,000. The stated goal of the policies will be to bridge and increase partnerships between institutions providing critical workforce development and training and our growing employers, particularly those requesting public financial support. Meet & Confer requirements may be structured similarly to those already in existence within the Department of Inclusion. A report is requested in 90 days.

t: Zero Tolerance policy for bigoted slurs by employees
rt: MOTION, WE MOVE for a Zero Tolerance policy for all City of Cincinnati employees or contractor/vendor while doing business with the City of Cincinnati in the case of any incident that involves the general public and a City of Cincinnati employee or contractor/vendor using a racial, religious, cultural or otherwise bigoted slur. Violation of this policy will lead to immediate termination of employment or termination of contract. In cases where City of Cincinnati employees use racial, religious, cultural or otherwise bigoted slurs towards each other, the incident will be referred to Human Resources and City Administration and subject to the penalties as outlined in Administrative Regulation 25 ("AR25"). (STATEMENT ATTACHED)
sm: Establish zero tolerance policy for City employees or contractors using bigoted slurs with immediate termination.

t: Implement citywide Parking Amnesty Program for unpaid tickets
rt: MOTION, submitted by Councilmembers Dennard & Young, RECOGNIZING that many residents face significant financial hardship that impacts their ability to pay fines and penalties imposed by the City of Cincinnati, and FURTHER RECOGNIZING that dealing with unpaid parking tickets is a serious burden that should be addressed by municipal government within means reasonable and appropriate, WE MOVE that the City Administration take all actions necessary and proper to implement a citywide Parking Amnesty Program. WE FURTHER MOVE that the duration of any such Parking Amnesty Program should be for at least one full calendar month, and serve the purpose of forgiving late fees and penalties associated with outstanding unpaid parking tickets, the spirit of forgiveness and to incentivize the payment of outstanding tickets, and collection of fees otherwise rendered near to impossible to collect. WE FURTHER MOVE that the City Administration report to Council on the feasibility and fiscal impact of implementing the following eligibility requirements for this program: 1. Individuals with parking violations issued prior to 2018 that are unpaid or partially unpaid 2. Individuals with towing and storage fees prior to 2016. WE FURTHER MOVE that the City Administration report to Council regarding any of its own recommendations for the timeline, budget structure and eligibility requirements of a Parking Amnesty Program, as well the status of implementations of the herein proposed framework for such a program, within 90 days of passage of this motion. WE FURTHER MOVE that the City Administration provide the offices of City Council with a copy of a draft implementation plan by May 1, 2019.
sm: Direct City Administration to implement month-long parking amnesty program forgiving late fees and penalties.

t: Rename fitness centers in honor of Patty Herlinger
rt: MOTION, submitted by Councilmembers Sittenfeld and Landsman WE MOVE that the fitness centers listed below be renamed in honor of Patty Herlinger. (BACKGROUND) Patty Herlinger-who tragically passed away on September 4, 2019-was a beloved, longtime City of Cincinnati employee who served Greater Cincinnati Water Works (GCWW), the Metropolitan Sewer District (MSD) and Risk Management over her 31-year career. An avid runner, Patty would often run up to 10 miles a day, and often with Recruits from the Cincinnati Fire Department. Over the course of her career, Patty successfully advocated for the establishment of fitness centers in GCWW's Chester Park Complex, GCWW's Richard Miller Treatment Plant, MSD's Creek Treatment Plant, MSD's Wastewater Collection Facility, and Centennial II.
sm: Rename five fitness centers honoring longtime city employee

t: Report on North Avondale intersection safety hazards
rt: MOTION, submitted by Vice Mayor Smitherman, WE MOVE the City Administration produce a report on the below intersections in North Avondale. 1. Clinton Springs Avenue & Reading Road: Residents report the left handed turn signal from Clinton Springs onto Reading Road is very short and the green light for drivers going west on Clinton Springs is even shorter. Drivers regularly run both lights and it's a safety hazard. 2. Red Bud Avenue & Mitchell Avenue: This intersection regularly has accidents. Drivers take the turn too fast, encounter the red light and either hit another car or the driver loses control. An additional concern is this intersection used as a bus stop and children wait at the curb for the bus. 3. Winding Way & Rose Hill: There are reports of drivers speeding along both roads.
sm: Assess traffic signal timing and safety issues at three intersections

t: Parking amnesty program for low-income residents
rt: MOTION, submitted by Councilmember Dennard, RECOGNIZING residents face significant financial hardship that impacts their ability to pay fines and penalties and that dealing with unpaid parking tickets poses a disproportionate economic burden on low-income households, WE MOVE the City Administration implement a Parking Amnesty program, taking into consideration recommendations from the City Manager received on June 12, 2019 (report attached), with the exception of a specific recommendation that was provided in the report; amnesty should be made available to all persons with eligible fines/fees, including those who are not current with all parking violation fees and fines incurred in years outside of the program parameters (2018-present); WE FURTHER MOVE that a parking amnesty program should serve the purpose of forgiving late fees and penalties associated with outstanding unpaid parking tickets, in the spirit of forgiveness and to incentivize the payment of outstanding tickets and the collection of outstanding fees otherwise rendered virtually impossible to collect. WE FURTHER MOVE the proposed parking amnesty program should be made available publicly for a period of no more than 90 days and that it should only apply to parking fines and towing/storage fees accrued on or before December 31, 2016. WE FURTHER MOVE for the City Administration to report on progress pertaining to the implementation of a parking amnesty program within 6-8 weeks of passage of this motion, with a recommended program start date of Spring 2020. (ATTACHMENT)
sm: Forgive late fees penalties on parking violations through 2016

t: Create separate inventory for City Council boards commissions
rt: MOTION, submitted by Councilmembers Dennard, Young, Seelbach and Landsman, WE MOVE that the City Administration create a separate inventory for City Council Commission and Board listings, where City Council has direct appointments to these board/commissions. This list should include, but is not limited to the: Salary History Working Group (to be housed on both the Board and Commission Inventory as well as the Equity webpages); Board of Housing Appeals; Internal Audit Committee; Any other board/commission that has an appointment by Council designated to it. Each of these pages should include the authority, contact, purpose, meeting schedule, board appointments (as well as their designated roles, if applicable), term length and list of past board members dating back to the origin of the board/commission. These pages should be consistent with the look and set-up of the CMO's Commission and Board Inventory to maintain consistency and ease of access to the information. WE FURTHER MOVE that the meeting times, locations and contact information for each board and commission are added to a public facing calendar with the board commissions appointed by the City Manager.
sm: Establish separate board commission inventory with appointments, contact info, meeting schedules

t: Review CMO appointed boards commissions website listings
rt: MOTION, submitted by Councilmembers Dennard, Young, Seelbach and Landsman, WE MOVE that the City Manager's office do a full review of the CMO Appointed Boards and Commissions listing on the City's website with the goal of relaying consistent information across all pages. Areas of attention include, but are not limited to: adding more detailed contact information to several listings so the public knows who to contact (and how to contact them) with questions about the board commissions; designating what role each appointee fills on the Equal Employment Opportunity Advisory Review Board and the Committee of Names (expand this to all listings that need this type of information); categorizing each board and commission either as a decision-making board/commission or advisory and further listing whether the board is voluntary or paid; reviewing the boards and commissions with open seats and getting those appointments filled with qualified and diverse appointments; adding links to each listing that references the Municipal Code, making it easier for the pub lic to find more information on the board/commission directly in the code; creating a public calendar that includes all meeting times, locations and contact information for each board and commission; updating each page to include information on every past member of the board and the years they served dating back to the origin of the board/commission; adding optional, self-identifying questions to the universal application with the goal of intentionally creating more diverse boards and commissions.
sm: Full review of board commission pages for consistency, diversity, accessibility improvements

t: Street Racing, Stunt Driving, Street Takeover Penalties
rt: ORDINANCE (EMERGENCY), submitted by Councilmember Jeffreys, from Emily Smart Woerner, City Solicitor, MODIFYING the provisions of Title V, “Traffic Code,” of the Cincinnati Municipal Code (“CMC”) by ORDAINING new Chapter 519, “Street Racing, Stunt Driving, and Street Takeover”; MODIFYING the provisions of Chapter 759, “Use of a Motor Vehicle to Facilitate a Prostitution or Drug Related Crime,” of the CMC by ORDAINING new Sections 759-6, “Use of a Motor Vehicle for Street Racing, Stunt Driving, and Street Takeover Prohibited”; 759-6-1, “Impoundment of Motor Vehicles Used to Facilitate Street Racing, Stunt Driving, and Street Takeover”; and 759-6-2, “Answer to Notice; Hearings for Motor Vehicles Impounded for Street Racing, Stunt Driving, and Street Takeover”; and by AMENDING Sections 759-1, “Legislative Findings”; 759-5, “Impoundment of Motor Vehicles Used to Facilitate Officer Evasion, Prostitution or Drug Related Crimes”; 759-7, “Answer to Notice; Hearings”; 759-9, “Posting Bond”; 759-11, “Default”; 759-13, “Appeal”; and 759-15, “Sale of Impounded Vehicles”; MODIFYING the provisions of Chapter 513, “Impoundment of Motor Vehicles,” of the CMC by AMENDING Sections 513-1, “Impoundment of Motor Vehicles,” and 513-11, “Sale of Impounded Vehicles”; and MODIFYING the provisions of Title XV, “Code Compliance and Hearings,” of the CMC by AMENDING Section 1501-11, “Class E Civil Offenses,” all to make participation in street racing, stunt driving, and street takeover a misdemeanor of the first degree; to make the use of a motor vehicle to facilitate the commission of a crime involving street racing, stunt driving, and street takeover a Class E Civil Offense; and to permit police officers to impound vehicles used in the commission of such offenses.
sm: Criminalize street racing, stunt driving, street takeovers as misdemeanors; permit vehicle impoundment.

t: FY 2027 General Fund Operating Budget Update
rt: ORDINANCE (EMERGENCY) submitted by Sheryl M. M. Long, City Manager, on 6/10/2026, PROVIDING for the appropriation of funds and authorization of expenditures from the General Fund 050 in the amount of $593,289,560 for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027, representing of the Recommended FY 2027 General Fund Operating Budget Update, per the attached Schedule of Appropriation, to provide for the current expenses and other expenses of the City; AUTHORIZING the transfer of $3,522,340 from the unappropriated surplus of General Fund 050 to the unappropriated surplus of Bond Retirement Fund 151 to pay the City’s FY 2027 General Fund debt service obligations related to the Ohio Police & Fire Pension Fund in the amount of $2,340,180 and the Early Retirement Incentive Program (“ERIP”) in the amount of $1,182,160; AUTHORIZING the transfer of $22,868,310 from the unappropriated surplus of General Fund 050 to the unappropriated surplus of Cincinnati Health District Fund 416 to provide for the FY 2027 General Fund Operating Budget Update portion of the expenses of the Cincinnati Health Department; AUTHORIZING the transfer of $1,007,960 from the unappropriated surplus of General Fund 050 to the unappropriated surplus of Citizens Job Fund 308 to provide resources for the Career Pathways Initiative; AUTHORIZING the transfer of $18,430 from the unappropriated surplus of General Fund 050 to the unappropriated surplus of Enterprise Technology Solutions Fund 702 to provide resources for debt service for the ERIP; AUTHORIZING the transfer of $160,000 from the unappropriated surplus of General Fund 050 to the unappropriated surplus of Qualified Employee Benefit Arrangement (QEBA) Fund 748 to provide resources for Contribution to Total Benefit Arrangement payments; AMENDING the sections of Chapter 307, “Classified Compensation Schedules,” of the Cincinnati Municipal Code regarding the compensation schedules of employees in Divisions 0, 5, 7 (LAW), 8, and 9 by applying a three percent wage adjustment for non-represented employees to constitute the new classification and salary range schedule for these classifications and to provide for wage adjustments effective June 21, 2026; REVISING the Department of Buildings and Inspections fee schedule to reflect the annual consumer price index adjustment of two and four tenths percent applied to fees charged for services related to property permitting and maintenance; t: Recognizing Human Rights Campaign 2026 Pride Month
rt: RESOLUTION, submitted by Councilmember Albi, from Emily Smart Woerner, City Solicitor, RECOGNIZING the Human Rights Campaign as a 2026 Pride Month honoree and EXPRESSING the appreciation of the Mayor and the Council of the City of Cincinnati for the Human Rights Campaign’s dedication to inclusion and equality for all.
sm: Recognition of Human Rights Campaign as Pride Month honoree for dedication to inclusion and equality.

t: Transfer funds for Roselawn summer activity event
rt: ORDINANCE (EMERGENCY), submitted by Vice Mayor Kearney, from Emily Smart Woerner, City Solicitor, AUTHORIZING the transfer of $10,000 from General Fund balance sheet reserve account no. 050x2581, “Reserve for Special Events Support,” to the unappropriated surplus of General Fund 050; AUTHORIZING the transfer of $10,000 from the unappropriated surplus of General Fund 050 to the unappropriated surplus of Recreation Special Activities Fund 323; and AUTHORIZING the transfer and appropriation of $10,000 from the unappropriated surplus of Recreation Special Activities Fund 323 to Cincinnati Recreation Commission non-personnel operating budget account no. 323x199x7400 to provide resources for the Roselawn New Prospect Baptist Church Summer Activity “Trigger Free Fridays” Event.
sm: Transfer $10,000 to support Trigger Free Fridays summer event at New Prospect Baptist Church.
